title: Replay export claims exact parity with a preview it does not match above 96
body:
## Summary
The grid replay export says the identical grid was previewed, but above 96 cells per side it ships a different layout.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/level-design/ProcgenGridReplayExport.tsx:41 says the export is the grid the preview showed, and :78 states "Exact by construction". generatePreview regenerates at the capped size (src/lib/level-design/procgen-preview.ts:107), so the two grids differ above 96. The parity sentence comes from layoutAgreement in lib, outside this context. Governing technique: seed-determinism-contract (a different parameter set is a different level).

## Flow
- Set grid 256x256
- Export grid for UE replay
- The artifact is a 256-side generation, not the 96-side grid on screen, under an "Exact by construction" line

## Expected impact
A designer replaying a large level gets rooms they never saw; the fix must keep the claim true at 96 and below.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the parity claim is true at every grid size
Before: tsx probe, 256x256 over 4 algorithms and 20 seeds each: room count differs on 29 of 80, connected verdict flips on 3 of 80
After: not measured: the claim would be conditional on the preview being uncapped
Method: probe - measured the divergence only; the wording fix was not applied because it lives in lib
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Component test: spec 128x128 must not render the unconditional parity line; spec 64x64 still does.

title: Layout remedies are verified on the capped preview, not the exported grid
body:
## Summary
Find a fix reports remedies as measured connected, but above 96 cells it measured a different grid from the one exported.

## Description
src/lib/level-design/layout-remedies.ts:135 runs generatePreview without an export-size cap, so the "regions === 1" proof applies to the preview only. The probe shows the connected verdict can flip between the two sizes. A fix could verify at export size within REMEDY_PREVIEW_BUDGET, or disclose the limit.

## Flow
- Open a large fragmented cellular level
- Apply a remedy listed as one region
- Export at full size, where the verdict can differ

## Expected impact
Designers stop trusting a green remedy that fails at export; verification at full size costs more per diagnosis.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a listed remedy holds on the shipped grid
Before: connected verdict flips on 3 of 80 256x256 samples (2 cellular, 1 perlin)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Harness over large specs: share of remedies still at one region when regenerated at MAX_EXPORT_SIZE, plus diagnosis time.

title: History Use seed leaves the room count, so it does not replay the run
body:
## Summary
Reusing a dungeon run restores its seed only, though the ledger stores the requested room count.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/level-design/ProcGenDungeonPanel.tsx:189 sets only the seed. The dispatch records params.roomCountRequested (src/lib/cli-task-handlers.ts procgenDungeon staticFields). seed-determinism-contract requires seed and parameter set together. Whether the button should replay or only reuse is a wording decision the fix must make.

## Flow
- Generate with 12 rooms and seed 42
- Change rooms to 6
- Use seed from history: rooms stays 6, so the layout differs

## Expected impact
A designer can return to a good dungeon in one click; legacy rows without the param must keep the current field.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a history row can reproduce its run
Before: by reading: 1 of 2 run inputs restored
After: predicted: 2 of 2 when the row recorded roomCountRequested
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Panel test with a mocked row: reuse sets both inputs, and a row without the param leaves rooms alone.

title: UE seed validation has no upper bound
body:
## Summary
validateSeed accepts any non-negative integer, including values beyond the 32-bit seed UE reads.

## Description
src/lib/level-design/run-params.ts:29 checks only the lower bound. The handoff treats the seed as uint32 read back as int32 (src/lib/level-design/procgen-spec.ts ueDungeonParamsFromSpec). A larger value reaches PROCGEN_SEED and the ledger unchanged. How the UE script parses it was not checked in this round.

## Flow
- Type 99999999999 as the seed
- Validation passes
- The ledger records a value UE may not have used

## Expected impact
History stays truthful about the seed; existing stored seeds are unaffected because only input changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every accepted seed is representable by the generator
Before: by reading: no upper bound in validateSeed
After: predicted: rejected above 4294967295
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Unit test on validateSeed at 4294967295 and 4294967296, after reading build_procgen_dungeon.py for its parse.

title: Spawn count and wave accept zero and negative values
body:
## Summary
The spawn number fields store whatever Number() returns, so a cleared field is 0 and negatives persist.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/level-design/RoomDetailPanel/SpawnEntriesPanel.tsx:73 and :85 use Number(e.target.value). The min attribute does not constrain typing. Clamping per keystroke would break typing, so validation belongs at commit (blur or debounce flush).

## Flow
- Clear the count field
- The buffered edit stores count 0
- The spawn row is saved with no enemies

## Expected impact
Generated spawn code gets valid counts; the commit-time clamp must not fight typing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - stored spawn rows are valid
Before: by reading: 2 unbounded fields per row
After: predicted: 0 after a commit-time clamp
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Panel test: clear then blur yields count >= 1, and typing 12 is not altered mid-entry.

title: Preview re-hashes the seed label instead of reading the resolved seed
body:
## Summary
The spec resolves seedValue once, then the preview hashes seedLabel again.

## Description
src/lib/level-design/procgen-spec.ts:248 passes the label and src/lib/level-design/procgen-preview.ts:109 hashes it. seed-determinism-contract names re-deriving at a call site as the way stages diverge. Both use one hashSeed today, so no divergence exists yet.

## Flow
- A spec reaches previewConfigFromSpec
- seedValue is dropped
- generatePreview derives it again

## Expected impact
Removes a second derivation of one quantity; PreviewConfig callers change, and output must stay identical.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one derivation of the resolved seed
Before: 2 derivation sites on the spec path
After: predicted: 1, with byte-identical grids
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
instrument: Grid hash comparison across algorithms and seeds before and after, plus enumerating PreviewConfig callers.

title: A stale export plan stays stale after undo restores its spec
body:
## Summary
Undoing back to the prepared spec still requires a re-prepare.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/level-design/ProceduralLevelWizard/exportFlow.ts:79 handles specChanged only from prepared or failed, so a stale flow whose key matches again never recovers. The cost is one extra click, and failed-origin plans would need their status kept to recover exactly.

## Flow
- Prepare an export
- Edit the seed: stale
- Undo: the spec matches but the plan remains stale

## Expected impact
Saves one click; re-preparing is always safe, so value is small.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a plan matching the live spec is sendable
Before: by reading: stale is terminal until re-prepare or cancel
After: predicted: prepared again when keys match
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Reducer test: prepared, specChanged(other), specChanged(original) returns prepared.

title: Pacing report filters and Jump buttons lack state and context
body:
## Summary
The rule select has no name, severity chips expose no pressed state, and every Jump button has the same name.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/level-design/PacingReportPanel.tsx:133 is a select with only a decorative icon beside it. SummaryChip at :192 shows the active filter by colour alone. Jump at :296 repeats per finding with no room named.

## Flow
- Tab through the report with a screen reader
- Hear an unnamed combobox and identical Jump buttons

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users can filter and navigate findings; no visual change.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - filter state and targets are announced
Before: by reading: 1 unnamed select, 0 chips with aria-pressed, Jump names not unique
After: predicted: 0 unnamed, all chips stateful, Jump names the room
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Component test counting unnamed controls, aria-pressed chips and duplicate button names.

title: Room detail toggles and generate button hide state or focus
body:
## Summary
Disclosure toggles lack aria-expanded, room-type buttons lack selection state, and the generate button removes its outline.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/level-design/RoomDetailPanel/index.tsx:234 and src/components/modules/content/level-design/RoomDetailPanel/SpawnEntriesPanel.tsx:31 toggle sections with no aria-expanded. Room-type buttons at index.tsx:119 show selection by colour. The generate button at index.tsx:267 has outline-none and no focus replacement.

## Flow
- Keyboard-tab to Execute Spawn Sequence
- No focus indicator appears

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users see focus and section state; visual change only on focus.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - state and focus are perceivable
Before: by reading: 2 toggles without aria-expanded, 8 type buttons without state, 1 suppressed outline
After: predicted: 0 of each
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Extend the sweep test with aria-expanded, aria-pressed and focus-ring assertions.

title: Difficulty colours are defined twice
body:
## Summary
DifficultyArcChart keeps its own copy of the difficulty colour map exported by RoomDetailPanel constants.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/level-design/DifficultyArcChart.tsx:9 and src/components/modules/content/level-design/RoomDetailPanel/constants.ts:23 hold the same five mappings. The chart copy is keyed by number, so an out-of-range difficulty gets an undefined stroke silently.

## Flow
- Change one map
- The chart and panel disagree on a threat colour

## Expected impact
One source for the colours; no visual change expected.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of the map
Before: 2 copies
After: predicted: 1
Method: simulation - read the path and walked the case; no isolated build was run in this round, which only built Lane A
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Grep count of the local map, plus a render assertion that stroke colours are unchanged.
